items.title: Chicken Biriyani
items.summary: A fragrant Kerala-style biryani made with marinated chicken, basmati rice, and whole spices cooked together for rich layered flavor. Medium • 60 mins • Non-Veg • One-pot / Dum option Ingredients Marinate the chicken with turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, pepper powder, salt, and curd.
items.content_html:
A fragrant Kerala-style biryani made with marinated chicken, basmati rice, and whole spices cooked together for rich layered flavor.


Medium • 60 mins • Non-Veg • One-pot / Dum option

Ingredients

  • Basmati rice – 2 cups    or jeerakasala rice for authentic Kerala taste)
  • Chicken – ½ kg
  • Turmeric powder – ½ tsp
  • Chilli powder – 1 tbsp(Adjust to taste)
  • Coriander powder – 1 tsp
  • Pepper powder – 1 tsp
  • Garam masala-1/2 tsp
  • Salt – 1 tsp (or to taste)
  • Curd (yogurt) – ¼ cup

Marinate the chicken with turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, pepper powder, salt, and curd. Keep aside for at least 30 minutes.

Vegetables & herbs

  • Onions – 2 large (sliced)
  • Tomatoes – 2 large (chopped)
  • Green chillies – 5
  • Ginger – 1-inch piece
  • Garlic – 10 cloves
  • Coriander leaves – 1 cup (chopped)
  • Mint leaves – ½ cup

Whole spices

  • Cloves – 3
  • Cardamom – 3
  • Cinnamon – ½-inch stick
  • Fennel seeds – ½ tsp
  • Mace – 1 (optional)

Other

  • Bay leaves – 1–2 (optional)
  • Lemon juice – 1 tbsp
  • Ghee – 1 tbsp
  • Water – 3¾ cups

Method

  1. Grind the ginger, garlic, green chillies, and whole spices into a paste.
  2. Heat oil and a little ghee in a pan. Sauté the sliced onions until soft and transparent.
  3. Add the ground paste and sauté for about 5 minutes until the raw smell disappears.
  4. Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they become soft and pulpy.
  5. Add the marinated chicken, along with coriander leaves and mint leaves. Mix well and sauté for about 7 minutes.
  6. Add 3¾ cups of water and bring to a boil. Then add the washed and drained rice.
  7. Add lemon juice, bay leaves (if using), 1 tbsp ghee, and adjust salt to taste.

Notes

Cooking options:

  • Pressure cooker: Cook for 1 whistle on medium flame.
  • Pot method: Cover with a lid and cook on medium flame until the water is absorbed and the rice is done.

Optional garnish:

  • Top with chopped coriander leaves, fried onions, cashews,

Layering (Dum method – optional):

  • You can cook the rice separately until 75% done( add salt to taste and lime juice 1 tsp)then layer it over 75% cooked chicken.    Cover tightly and cook on very low heat for 20 minutes (place a fry pan ( cast iron pan is better) underneath to avoid burning). Add garnishes while layering. And sprinkle a pinch of turmeric mixed in 1 tbs water for colour

items.title: Tandoori Masala
items.summary: A bold, smoky spice blend for classic tandoori-style dishes. Medium • 20 mins • Veg • Spice Mix • Homemade Ingredients 1/4 cup coriander seeds (or 3 tbsp coriander powder) 1 tbsp cumin seeds 2 tsp peppercorns 10 green cardamom 2 black cardamom (optional) 2…
items.content_html:
A bold, smoky spice blend for classic tandoori-style dishes.

Medium • 20 mins • Veg • Spice Mix • Homemade

Ingredients

  • 1/4 cup coriander seeds (or 3 tbsp coriander powder)
  • 1 tbsp cumin seeds
  • 2 tsp peppercorns
  • 10 green cardamom
  • 2 black cardamom (optional)
  • 2 inch cinnamon piece
  • 2 pieces mace
  • 1 tsp nutmeg powder
  • 10 Kashmiri red chillies (or 3 tbsp chilli powder)
  • 2 tsp kasoori methi (dry fenugreek leaves)

Method

  1. Dry roast coriander seeds, cumin seeds, peppercorns, cloves, cardamom, cinnamon, and mace on low heat for 2–3 minutes until fragrant.
  2. If using coriander powder or chilli powder instead of whole spices, add them  after switching off the flame.
  3. Add kasuri methi and nutmeg powder. Let everything cool completely.
  4. Grind into a fine powder.
  5. Mix well and store in an airtight container.

Notes  

  • Adjust chilli based on spice and colour preference.
  • Store in a cool, dry place or refrigerate for longer freshness.

items.content_html:
Aromatic homemade spice blend roasted and freshly ground.

Easy • 15 mins • Veg • Spice Mix • Homemade

Ingredients

  • 50 g fennel seeds (about 1/2 cup)
  • 20 g cardamom (about 1/4 cup)
  • 20 g cloves
  • 20 g cinnamon

Method

  1. Dry roast all the spices in a frying pan on low heat until aromatic.
  2. Let the spices cool completely.
  3. Grind into a fine powder.
  4. Store in an airtight container.

Notes

  • Store in the freezer to maintain freshness and aroma for longer.
  • Ensure spices are completely cool before grinding to avoid moisture.

items.title: Split Green Gram Payasam (Moong Dal Payasam)
items.summary: A traditional, rich payasam made with roasted split green gram, jaggery, coconut milk, and aromatic spices. Easy • 40–50 mins • Dessert • Veg • Serve warm Cook the dal Prepare the jaggery Finish the payasam Reduce the heat and stir in the thick coconut…
items.content_html:
A traditional, rich payasam made with roasted split green gram, jaggery, coconut milk, and aromatic spices.

Easy • 40–50 mins • Dessert • Veg • Serve warm

Ingredients

  • 1 cup split green gram (moong dal)
  • 4 cups lukewarm water, for cooking the dal
  • 300–400 g jaggery (adjust to taste)
  • 1 cup water, for melting the jaggery
  • ½ cup thick coconut milk
  • 1 tbsp coconut milk, to add to the cooking water
  • 2–3 tbsp ghee
  • 10 cashew nuts
  • 10 raisins
  • ½ tsp cardamom powder
  • ¼ tsp dry ginger powder

Method

Cook the dal

  1. Dry-roast the split green gram in a pan over medium-low heat until the raw smell disappears. Do not let it turn brown.
  2. Transfer the roasted dal to a pressure cooker.
  3. Add the 4 cups of water and 1 tbsp coconut milk.
  4. Pressure-cook until the first whistle, then cook for another 5 minutes over low heat.
  5. Switch off the heat and allow the pressure to release naturally.
  6. Open the cooker and check that the dal is soft.

Prepare the jaggery

  1. Melt the jaggery in 1 cup water over low heat.
  2. Strain the melted jaggery syrup to remove any impurities.
  3. Add the jaggery syrup to the cooked dal.
  4. Simmer for about 5 minutes, stirring gently.

Finish the payasam

  1. Reduce the heat and stir in the thick coconut milk.
  2. Add the cardamom powder and dry ginger powder. Mix well.
  3. Heat the ghee in a small pan.
  4. Fry the cashews until golden, then add the raisins and fry until they puff up.
  5. Pour the fried nuts, raisins, and ghee into the payasam. Mix gently and serve warm.

Notes

  • Do not brown the dal while roasting, as this can change the flavour.
  • Strain the jaggery syrup before adding it to the dal.
  • After adding the thick coconut milk, heat gently and avoid vigorous boiling.
  • Adjust the jaggery according to your preferred sweetness.

items.title: Vermicelli Payasam (Semiya Payasam)
items.summary: A comforting Indian milk dessert made with roasted vermicelli, cardamom, cashews, and raisins. Easy • 25–30 mins • Dessert • Veg • Serve warm or chilled Ingredients 1 cup vermicelli (semiya) 1 litre milk 3–4 tbsp sugar (adjust to taste) 2 tbsp ghee 10–12 cashew…
items.content_html:
A comforting Indian milk dessert made with roasted vermicelli, cardamom, cashews, and raisins.

Easy • 25–30 mins • Dessert • Veg • Serve warm or chilled

Ingredients

  • 1 cup vermicelli (semiya)
  • 1 litre milk
  • 3–4 tbsp sugar (adjust to taste)
  • 2 tbsp ghee
  • 10–12 cashew nuts
  • 10–15 raisins
  • 3–4 cardamom pods, crushed
  • A few saffron strands (optional)

Method

  1. Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a pan.
  2. Add the vermicelli and roast over low heat until lightly golden. Skip this step if using pre-roasted vermicelli.
  3. In another pot, bring the milk to a boil, stirring occasionally to prevent it from sticking.
  4. Add the roasted vermicelli to the milk.
  5. Cook over medium-low heat for 8–10 minutes, or until the vermicelli is soft.
  6. Add the sugar and crushed cardamom. Stir well and simmer for another 3–5 minutes.
  7. In a small pan, heat the remaining ghee.
  8. Fry the cashews until golden, then add the raisins and fry until they puff up.
  9. Add the fried nuts, raisins, and ghee to the payasam. Mix well.
  10. Add saffron strands, if using, and serve.

Notes

  • Adjust the sugar to taste.
  • Stir frequently while cooking the vermicelli to prevent it from sticking to the bottom.
  • The payasam thickens as it cools. Add a little warm milk if you prefer a thinner consistency.

items.title: Rice Payasam
items.summary: A traditional, creamy rice pudding simmered in milk and flavoured with cardamom, cashews, and raisins. Easy • 40 mins • Dessert • Veg • Serve warm or chilled Ingredients ½ cup raw rice, preferably small-grain rice 1 litre milk ¾ cup sugar 1 tbsp ghee…
items.content_html:
A traditional, creamy rice pudding simmered in milk and flavoured with cardamom, cashews, and raisins.

Easy • 40 mins • Dessert • Veg • Serve warm or chilled

Ingredients

  • ½ cup raw rice, preferably small-grain rice
  • 1 litre milk
  • ¾ cup sugar
  • 1 tbsp ghee
  • Cashew nuts, as needed
  • Raisins, as needed
  • A pinch of salt
  • Powdered cardamom, to taste

Method

  1. If using basmati rice, pulse it briefly in a mixer to break the grains into smaller pieces. Do not grind it into a powder.
  2. Add the rice and milk to a large, heavy-bottomed pot.
  3. Cook over medium-low heat for about 30 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent the milk from sticking or burning.
  4. Continue cooking until the rice is soft and the payasam reaches your preferred consistency.
  5. Add the sugar and stir until dissolved.
  6. Add a pinch of salt and powdered cardamom. Mix well.
  7. Heat the ghee in a small pan.
  8. Fry the cashews until golden, then add the raisins and fry until they puff up.
  9. Pour the fried nuts, raisins, and ghee over the payasam. Mix gently and serve.

Notes

  • Use a large pot, as milk can rise quickly when heated.
  • Stir frequently, especially near the bottom of the pot.
  • The payasam thickens further as it cools. Add a little warm milk if needed before serving.

items.title: Green Tea Pudding
items.summary: A delicate, creamy milk pudding flavoured with matcha green tea. Easy • 20 mins preparation • 2–3 hrs chilling • Dessert • Veg • Chilled Prepare the china grass Prepare the matcha Prepare the milk mixture Set the pudding Pour into individual moulds or a…
items.content_html:
A delicate, creamy milk pudding flavoured with matcha green tea.

Easy • 20 mins preparation • 2–3 hrs chilling • Dessert • Veg • Chilled

Ingredients

  • 2 cups milk
  • ½ cup water, for soaking the china grass
  • 8–10 g china grass (agar-agar)
  • 4–5 tbsp sugar (adjust to taste)
  • 1–1½ tsp matcha (green tea powder)
  • 2 tbsp condensed milk (optional, for creaminess)

Method

Prepare the china grass

  1. Cut the china grass into small pieces, if necessary, and soak it in ½ cup water for 10–15 minutes.
  2. Heat gently until fully dissolved, ensuring no strands remain.

Prepare the matcha

  1. Place the matcha powder in a small bowl.
  2. Add 2–3 tbsp warm milk and whisk until smooth and free of lumps.

Prepare the milk mixture

  1. Heat the milk, sugar, and condensed milk in a saucepan.
  2. Stir until the sugar dissolves. Avoid boiling vigorously.
  3. Add the dissolved china grass to the hot milk and stir continuously for 2–3 minutes.
  4. Add the matcha mixture and stir until evenly combined.

Set the pudding

  1. Pour into individual moulds or a shallow tray.
  2. Allow it to cool at room temperature.
  3. Refrigerate for 2–3 hours, or until firm.

Notes

  • Adjust the amount of matcha according to your preferred green tea flavour.
  • Whisk the matcha with warm milk before adding it to prevent lumps.
  • Agar-agar powder can be used instead of china grass; follow the package instructions.

items.title: Tender Coconut Pudding
items.summary: A refreshing, creamy pudding made with tender coconut water and soft coconut flesh. Easy • 20 mins preparation • 2–3 hrs chilling • Dessert • Veg • Chilled Prepare the china grass Prepare the milk mixture Add the coconut Set the pudding Pour into a…
items.content_html:
A refreshing, creamy pudding made with tender coconut water and soft coconut flesh.

Easy • 20 mins preparation • 2–3 hrs chilling • Dessert • Veg • Chilled

Ingredients

  • 2 cups tender coconut water
  • 1 cup tender coconut flesh (soft malai), chopped or lightly blended
  • 1 cup milk
  • 8–10 g china grass (agar-agar)
  • ½ cup water, for soaking the china grass
  • 4–5 tbsp sugar (adjust to taste)
  • 2–3 tbsp condensed milk (optional)

Method

Prepare the china grass

  1. Cut the china grass into small pieces, if necessary, and soak it in ½ cup water for 10–15 minutes.
  2. Heat gently until completely dissolved, stirring to remove any strands.

Prepare the milk mixture

  1. Heat the milk, sugar, and condensed milk in a saucepan.
  2. Stir until the sugar dissolves. There is no need to boil vigorously.
  3. Add the dissolved china grass to the hot milk and stir continuously for 2–3 minutes.

Add the coconut

  1. Switch off the heat and allow the mixture to cool slightly while remaining liquid.
  2. Stir in the tender coconut water and coconut flesh gently until combined.

Set the pudding

  1. Pour into a mould or glass dish.
  2. Allow it to cool at room temperature.
  3. Refrigerate for 2–3 hours, or until set.
  4. Cut into cubes or scoop gently and serve chilled.

Notes

  • Do not add the coconut water while the milk mixture is boiling vigorously.
  • For a clear jelly-style pudding, omit the milk and condensed milk and use coconut water, sugar, and agar-agar instead.
  • Adjust the sugar according to the natural sweetness of the coconut water.

items.title: Marble Pudding
items.summary: A beautiful two-tone milk pudding with delicate vanilla and chocolate swirls. Easy • 20 mins preparation • 2–3 hrs chilling • Dessert • Veg • Chilled Prepare the china grass Prepare the milk mixture Create the marble effect Set the pudding Allow it to cool…
items.content_html:
A beautiful two-tone milk pudding with delicate vanilla and chocolate swirls.

Easy • 20 mins preparation • 2–3 hrs chilling • Dessert • Veg • Chilled

Ingredients

  • 1 litre milk
  • 10 g china grass (agar-agar)
  • ½ cup water, for soaking the china grass
  • 5–6 tbsp sugar (adjust to taste)
  • 1 tsp vanilla essence
  • 1 tbsp cocoa powder
  • 3–4 tbsp condensed milk (optional, for richness)

Method

Prepare the china grass

  1. Cut the china grass into small pieces, if necessary, and soak it in ½ cup water for 10–15 minutes.
  2. Heat gently until completely dissolved, stirring to ensure no strands remain.

Prepare the milk mixture

  1. Heat the milk, sugar, and condensed milk in a saucepan.
  2. Stir until the sugar dissolves. Avoid boiling vigorously.
  3. Add the dissolved china grass to the hot milk, stirring continuously for 2–3 minutes.

Create the marble effect

  1. Divide the mixture equally between two bowls.
  2. Add the vanilla essence to one portion.
  3. Mix the cocoa powder with a little warm milk to form a smooth paste, then stir it into the second portion.
  4. Pour a ladleful of the white mixture into a mould, followed by some chocolate mixture.
  5. Continue alternating the two mixtures.
  6. Gently swirl a skewer or knife through the mixture to create a marble pattern. Do not overmix.

Set the pudding

  1. Allow it to cool at room temperature.
  2. Refrigerate for 2–3 hours, or until completely set.

Notes

  • Agar-agar powder can be used instead of china grass; follow the package instructions for the appropriate quantity.
  • Work quickly while the mixtures are still pourable, as agar-agar begins to set as it cools.
  • Do not over-swirl, or the marble pattern may disappear

items.title: Caramel Custard Pudding
items.summary: Ingredients For the custard 2 cups milk 5 eggs 10 tbsp sugar 1 tbsp vanilla essence For the caramel 8 tbsp sugar A little water, just enough to help dissolve the sugar Method Prepare the Caramel Add the sugar and a little water to a…
items.content_html:
Ingredients

For the custard

  • 2 cups milk
  • 5 eggs
  • 10 tbsp sugar
  • 1 tbsp vanilla essence
  • For the caramel
  • 8 tbsp sugar
  • A little water, just enough to help dissolve the sugar

Method

Prepare the Caramel

  1. Add the sugar and a little water to a saucepan.
  2. Heat over medium heat until the sugar dissolves and turns golden brown.
  3. Carefully pour the caramel into the pudding mould, tilting the mould to coat the bottom. Set aside.

Prepare the Custard

  1. In a bowl, beat the eggs gently.
  2. Add the sugar and mix until dissolved.
  3. Add the vanilla essence and milk. Mix well.
  4. Pour the custard mixture into the caramel-lined mould. For a smoother pudding, strain the mixture before pouring.

Steam the Pudding

  1. Place the mould in a steamer and steam over low to medium heat until the custard is set. The time will depend on the mould size.
  2. Insert a toothpick or skewer into the centre. It should come out mostly clean, with the custard set.
  3. Switch off the heat and allow the pudding to cool.
  4. Run a knife around the edges of the mould.
  5. Place a serving plate over the mould and carefully invert it.
  6. Refrigerate until thoroughly chilled before serving.

Notes

  • Be careful when handling hot caramel, as it can cause severe burns.
  • Avoid beating too much air into the eggs to prevent bubbles in the pudding.
  • For a smooth texture, steam gently rather than allowing the water to boil vigorously.
